title: IRGC Claims Strikes on Two US Patriot Radars in Bahrain
summary: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims it struck two US Patriot air defense radars at bases in Bahrain with missiles and drones. The claim rests on an IRGC statement, and no independent source describes radar damage. Bahraini authorities separately report a fire at an industrial facility after an Iranian attack.
contents:
## Event

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claims that its Aerospace Force struck two US Patriot air defense radars at the Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain with a combined missile and drone operation. The claim appears in an IRGC public relations statement that Iranian outlets published on the evening of November 21, 2026, UTC. The statement says the operation responded to US escort operations and to US drone violations of Iranian airspace.

## Location and Time

The statement names Riffa Air Base and Awali in Bahrain. The geographic point represents Bahrain as a whole because both named sites lie within the same small island country, and no single focal site appears in the reporting. The earliest timestamped copy of the IRGC statement found during checking appeared on Defapress at 20:15 UTC, derived from its stated 23:45 Tehran time. Clash Report reposted the claim at 20:17 UTC.

## Evidence

The primary source comprises the IRGC statement, reproduced in Persian by Defapress and Tasnim News Agency. Clash Report reposted the claim in English. An Al Jazeera live report from the same day, citing Fars, describes IRGC attacks on the Sheikh Isa and Juffair bases. The same report quotes Bahraini authorities who say an industrial facility got hit by an Iranian attack and caught fire. These independent reports document an attack and a fire in Bahrain that evening. None of them independently describes damage to Patriot radars. The US military has not addressed the radar claim in the sources checked.

## Allied Relevance

Reported strikes on Patriot radars at US bases in Bahrain bear on US air defense posture and force protection near the Strait of Hormuz. Bahrain hosts the US Navy Fifth Fleet, so a reported attack on radar systems there matters to United States and allied planners tracking Gulf escalation. The claim also shows how the IRGC frames its operations against US forces, which informs threat assessments.

## Confidence and Gaps

Confidence remains low to moderate because a conflict party issued the radar claim and no independent source describes radar damage. The IRGC attack and the Bahraini facility fire rest on separate reporting. Gaps include the lack of any damage assessment, the absence of a US or Bahraini statement on the radar claim in the sources checked, and an Al Mayadeen live-ticker entry that shows a time without a stated time zone. If that entry uses Beirut time, the first IRGC report would sit about five minutes earlier than the Defapress copy.
